subject: Clarify territorial data use, no-train commitment, and prompt/response rights for pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <contracts@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot DPA questions: training opt-out, ownership, and territory

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we spin up the 6-week pilot, our legal and security teams asked for a few clarifications so we can approve the SOW and run procurement. High level asks:

1) No-training commitment: can Redwood commit in the DPA that customer data sent to hosted endpoints will not be used to improve or update any shared models ("no-train")? If so, what operational controls and attestations will you provide?

2) Prompt/response ownership: Aurora needs explicit language that prompts and generated responses from our tenant are owned by Aurora and are exportable on request. Does Redwood require any derivative license for model improvement?

3) Subprocessors & data transfers: please provide a list of subprocessors and clarify whether any cross-border transfers to non-EEA regions will occur for processing. For the pilot we would prefer EU-only residency or onshore routing options.

4) Evidence: our auditors will want SOC2 + attestation that no adaptive training occurs, plus an export flow for transcripts and KV caching behavior.

Attached is our standard DPA draft (Aurora_DPA_Draft_v1.1.pdf) with some placeholders. Can you review and indicate which items Redwood can accept, which need redlines, and provide an evidence pack?

Appreciate a reply by EOD Wednesday so procurement can stay on schedule.

Thanks,
Sarah Turner
Senior PM, Clinical Integrations
Aurora Health

Attachments: Aurora_DPA_Draft_v1.1.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions: training opt-out, ownership, and territory

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Quick summary of what we can commit for the pilot and what we will need to propose as redlines:

- No-training: Redwood can commit to a strict operational "no-train" toggle for your tenant on hosted and dedicated offerings for the duration of the pilot. We provide an attestation letter and an ops runbook showing how we isolate tenant interactions (ephemeral KV, disabled adaptive retraining pipelines).

- Ownership: We are willing to accept language confirming Aurora retains ownership of prompts and generated responses. We will request standard limited rights to use aggregated telemetry (latency/quality metrics) that are non-identifying. No derivative license will be required for model improvement when the no-train toggle is enabled.

- Subprocessors & transfers: we can offer EU-only processing by routing your requests to our Frankfurt (eu-central) pool and restricting backups to EU storage for the pilot. I will loop in David from Security to surface the subprocessor inventory and SOC2 artifacts.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We will prepare a redline of your DPA (see attached placeholder: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v1.1.pdf).
2) David will provide the subprocessor CSV and SOC2 summary.
3) If that looks good, Marissa from Customer Success will schedule a handoff to onboarding for exportability test runs (SFTP/API).

I can get the redlines + attestation by EOD Wednesday. Would a Thursday technical call (30m) with Security + Legal work for you?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v1.1.pdf

From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <contracts@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions: training opt-out, ownership, and territory

Jonas —

Great, appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from legal:

- Can the attestation explicitly state that no retained learning artifacts (model checkpoints, fine-tune inputs) will be derived from Aurora tenant data while the toggle is enabled? A sentence in the DPA is ideal rather than a separate note.

- On exportability: we need transcripts and a machine-readable audit log for a sample window (first 30 days) exported via SFTP. We also need confirmation that ephemeral KV cache is cleared per-session and not persisted beyond the transaction unless we opt in.

- Subprocessors: can Redwood provide a timeline for any planned subprocessor changes during the pilot (advance notice + ability to object)?

Legal has a DocuSign that they prefer to use — I will forward once you confirm the core clauses.

If you can confirm the explicit sentence about no retained learning artifacts and the SFTP export path, we can move forward with procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah

Quoted: 
> On Mon, May 4, 2027 at 11:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> > I will loop in David from Security to surface the subprocessor inventory and SOC2 artifacts.
> >
> > Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v1.1.pdf

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@aurorahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions: training opt-out, ownership, and territory

Hi Sarah / Jonas —

Following up with the technical and compliance details you requested:

- Subprocessor inventory: attached is our current subprocessors CSV (redwood_subprocessors_inventory.csv). For the pilot we will gate processing to EU-only compute (Frankfurt) and EU storage. No US-based analytics pipelines will touch Aurora tenant data while the pilot no-train toggle is enabled.

- No retained-learning artifacts: we can add explicit language to the DPA: "Redwood will not retain model checkpoints, training datasets, derivative fine-tunes, or any artifacts that could be used to update or improve model weights derived from Aurora Health tenant data during the pilot period when the no-training toggle is engaged."

- KV cache behavior: by default Redis-based KV caches are ephemeral per-session and TTL'd; for added assurance we can disable prefix caching for your tenant and provide logs showing cache eviction parity during the sample window.

- SOC2 & evidence: we can provide our SOC2 Type II summary and a scoped attestation stating no adaptive training occurs for the pilot. For procurement/audit, we will provide an encrypted bundle via the secure drive link and a statement-of-facts signed by the Security lead.

- Subprocessor change control: we can commit to 30 days advance notice for any non-security-critical subprocessor changes and provide an objection window for contractual reviews.

I'll attach the CSV and a short attestation stub; happy to run through anything during the call.

-David
David Kim
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_inventory.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Legal Team <contracts@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions: training opt-out, ownership, and territory

Sarah —

Thanks — great progress. Confirming the explicit clause David proposed will be inserted into the DPA redline and the SFTP export path + sample audit logs are available for your onboarding team to test.

Proposed next steps:
- We will finalize Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v1.2.pdf (with the no-retained-artifacts sentence) and send it to your contracts address by EOD today.
- Marissa will schedule a 30-minute technical call on Thursday 11:00 AM CET / 2:00 AM PST to validate routing to Frankfurt and run an export test.
- Procurement: once DocuSign is ready from Aurora, we will accept the executed DPA and enable the no-train toggle for the pilot environment.

If that timeline works I will loop in our onboarding lead and send calendar invites. Looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Jonas

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v1.2.pdf
